# Wizz.js — full reference for language models

> Wizz.js is a zero-dependency, full-stack JavaScript framework. Single-file `.wizz` components compile ahead of time to plain DOM creation/update code and statically scoped CSS. Pages server-render by default and hydrate in the browser, with no Virtual DOM, no npm runtime packages, and built-in server API routes.

Versions covered: compiler 1.24.0, syntax 1.6.0, output 1.13.0 (`wizz --version`).
Human-readable docs: /docs/getting-started. Index: /llms.txt. Source: https://github.com/duncantidd/wizz.js

Wizz.js is NOT React, Vue, or Svelte. Its template grammar is deliberately tiny and statically analyzable, and the compiler rejects most idioms from other frameworks with a stable diagnostic code. When in doubt, compute it in `<script>` and reference the result by name.

---

## 1. Install and project layout

Requirements: Node.js 18+, curl and tar (installer only), an evergreen browser.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/duncantidd/wizz.js/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | bash
wizz init my-app
cd my-app && wizz dev          # http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

The CLI installs to `~/.local/share/wizz` with a launcher in `~/.local/bin`. Nothing is added to the project's `node_modules`.

```text
my-app/
├── index.html                 # Document shell: <div id="app"></div> + /runtime/main.js
├── App.css                    # Global tokens, reset, layout
└── src/
    ├── App.wizz               # Landing page → /
    ├── pages/Home.wizz        # Routed page → /home
    ├── components/Card.wizz   # Imported component
    └── server/api/health.js   # Server handler → /api/health
```

That is the sample project. From 1.24.0, on a terminal, `wizz init` first asks `Bootstrap with sample code? [Y/n]`; answering `n` (or passing `--bare`) writes a bare project instead: `index.html` with no stylesheet link, a placeholder `src/App.wizz`, and a `README.md`, with no `App.css`, components, pages, or API handler. Without a terminal (CI, pipes, agent shells) or with `--json`, init never asks and writes the sample project; pass `--bare` to get the bare one.

You edit `index.html`, `App.css`, `src/**/*.wizz`, and `src/server/api/*.js`. `dist/` is generated and disposable: never edit it.

---

## 2. Anatomy of a component

A `.wizz` file is one component: a template with exactly one native root element, plus at most one each of `<script>`, `<wizz:head>`, and `<wizz:style>`.

```html
<script>
  import Avatar from "./Avatar.wizz";

  export let user;               // prop (read-only in this component)
  let expanded = false;          // reactive state

  function toggle() {
    expanded = !expanded;
  }
</script>

<wizz:head>
  <title>{user.name} - Profile</title>
</wizz:head>

<article class="profile">
  <Avatar src={user.avatar} />
  <h2>{user.name}</h2>
  <button on:click={toggle} aria-expanded={expanded}>Details</button>
</article>

<wizz:style>
  .profile { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }
  h2 { margin: 0; }              /* scoped: other components' h2s are untouched */
</wizz:style>
```

- Template: exactly one native root element. Wrap siblings in one element.
- `<script>`: top-level `let` is reactive state, `export let` declares a prop, named functions are handlers, `onMount`/`onDestroy` register hooks with no import.
- `<wizz:head>`: only `<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>`.
- `<wizz:style>`: raw CSS scoped to this component. A plain `<style>` element is rejected (WIZZ-P020).
- Keep files LF-only (hydration compares template whitespace exactly).

---

## 3. Template expressions

`{...}` accepts a JavaScript expression subset (compiler 1.23.0+; precedence follows JavaScript):

1. Identifiers and member access: `{title}`, `{user.profile.name}`
2. Literals: `{"v1.0"}`, `{42}`, `{1.5}`, `{true}`, `{null}`
3. Arithmetic `+ - * /` and parentheses: `{(count + 1) * 2}`, `{"card " + kind}` (`+` also concatenates strings)
4. Comparisons: `===`, `!==`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
5. Logic and unary: `&&`, `||`, `!`, `-`
6. The conditional: `{count === 1 ? "item" : "items"}`, nestable
7. Calls of a script function or a method: `{plural(items.length)}`, `{name.trim().toUpperCase()}`

Still WIZZ-P033: indexing (`a[0]`), `==`/`!=`, `??`, `?.`, template literals, arrow functions, array/object literals, and calling a call result (`f()()`, WIZZ-P059). `++`/`--` are WIZZ-P056. An expression that calls may not mention `eval`, `Function`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `setTimeout`, or `setInterval` (WIZZ-P060).

A call re-renders only when a reactive name passed to it changes: `{plural(items.length)}` follows `items`; `{plural()}` reading `items` inside the function renders once. Anything that needs a loop, an arrow, or statements stays in the script.

Before 1.23.0 the grammar was only identifiers, member access, integer and string literals, arithmetic, and `===`; on older compilers compute everything else in the script.

```html
<script>
  let user = { name: "Ada", role: "admin" };
  let items = ["a", "b", "c"];

  let greeting = "Welcome back, " + user.name;
  function plural(n) { return n === 1 ? "item" : "items"; }
</script>

<section>
  <h2>{greeting}</h2>
  <p class={user.role === "admin" ? "badge admin" : "badge"}>{user.name}</p>
  {#if items.length > 0 && user.role === "admin"}
    <p>{items.length} {plural(items.length)}</p>
  {/if}
</section>
```

Text output escapes `&`, `<`, `>`; attribute values also escape `"`. HTML entities are not decoded in templates: to show a literal `<script>` in prose, write `{"<script>"}`.

Avoid empty-string text interpolations in server-rendered components: an empty text node does not survive HTML parsing, so hydration falls back to a client render. Initialize display strings to something visible.

---

## 4. Dynamic attributes

Bind an attribute by making its ENTIRE, UNQUOTED value an expression.

```html
<script>
  let active = true;
  let name = "Ada";
  let cardClass = active ? "card is-active" : "card";   // compose in the script
  let profileHref = "/users/" + name.toLowerCase();
</script>

<div class={cardClass}>
  <a href={profileHref}>Profile</a>
  <input value={name} checked={active} disabled={false} aria-label={name} />
</div>
```

- WRONG: `class="card {state}"` or `href="{url}"`. Quoted values are static: from 1.22.1 the compiler rejects `{expression}` inside them with WIZZ-P055 (older compilers rendered the braces literally, silently). Use one expression for the whole value: `class={"card " + state}` or a precomputed `class={cardClass}`.
- `value`, `checked`, and `disabled` update as DOM properties.
- From 1.21.0, HTML boolean attributes (`hidden`, `required`, `readonly`, `open`, `inert`, `multiple`, `selected`, `autofocus`, and the rest of the HTML list) are present when the value is truthy and removed when it is falsy: `hidden={isValid}` shows the element while `isValid` is `false`. Any other dynamic attribute is removed for `null`/`undefined` and otherwise set to `String(value)`, so `false` renders `"false"` and `aria-expanded={open}` stays correct. To drop a non-boolean attribute, hold `null` in state. Server rendering and hydration follow the same rules.
- Before 1.21.0, every name other than `value`/`checked`/`disabled` was written with `setAttribute(name, String(value))` and never removed: `hidden={false}` still hid the element and `undefined` rendered as `"undefined"`. On those compilers, toggle presence with a bound class and CSS.
- Two-way inputs: `bind:value={name}` / `bind:checked={done}` (1.23.0+, section 8). Before 1.23.0, `bind:value` silently became a plain attribute; pair `value={name}` with an `on:input` handler there.

---

## 5. Props

The child declares props with `export let`; the parent passes them as attributes on the component tag.

```html
<!-- Greeting.wizz -->
<script>
  export let name = "Guest";   // default when the parent omits it
  export let count;            // undefined unless passed
</script>

<p>Hello {name}, clicked {count} times</p>
```

```html
<!-- App.wizz -->
<script>
  import Greeting from "./components/Greeting.wizz";
  let clicks = 0;

  function click() {
    clicks += 1;
  }
</script>

<main>
  <Greeting name="Ada" count={clicks} emphasized />
  <button on:click={click}>Click</button>
</main>
```

- Static attributes pass strings, bare attributes pass `true`, `{expressions}` pass values that update when their dependencies change.
- New values arrive through `setProps()`; the child re-renders in place and keeps its DOM and internal state.
- Props are read-only in the child: assigning one is WIZZ-G015. Copy into a local `let` if you need to change it.
- One prop per `export let` (WIZZ-P038). Prop names may not start with `__wizz` or use a name reserved in section 7 (WIZZ-G025).
- Omitted prop or explicit `undefined` → default. Undeclared attributes are ignored.

---

## 6. Composition and imports

```html
<script>
  import SearchBar from "./SearchBar.wizz";
  let query = "";

  // Children talk to parents through callback props.
  function handleSearch(next) {
    query = next;
  }
</script>

<div class="toolbar">
  <SearchBar onSearch={handleSearch} placeholder="Filter…" />
</div>
```

- Default imports of a relative `.wizz` path only, each on its own line (WIZZ-G016).
- Render components as self-closing tags inside a native element (WIZZ-G010).
- No children or slots: `<Card><p>x</p></Card>` is WIZZ-G008. Pass content through props.
- No `on:` directives on component tags (WIZZ-G011). Pass a callback prop.
- No components inside `{#each}` (WIZZ-G004).
- Destroying a parent destroys every imported child.

---

## 7. Reactivity

Every top-level `let` in `<script>` is reactive. `const` renders once.

```html
<script>
  let count = 0;
  let user = { name: "Ada" };
  const LIMIT = 10;

  function increment() {
    if (count < LIMIT) {
      count += 1;
    }
  }

  function rename(next) {
    user = { ...user, name: next };
  }
</script>

<main>
  <p>{user.name} clicked {count} times</p>
  <button on:click={increment}>+1</button>
</main>
```

Updates are batched: each assignment marks its variable, and one DOM update runs on the next microtask with every mark combined.

Which mutations are tracked:

```js
// Tracked: statement-level assignments and updates, also inside callbacks
count = count + 1;
count += 1;
count++;
user.name = "Grace";              // property chains mark the root (user)
items = [...items, next];
setTimeout(() => { status = "done"; }, 500);
onMount(() => { ready = true; });

// NOT tracked
items.push(next);                 // method call: reassign the array instead
log(count = 5);                   // assignment inside an expression: warning WIZZ-G026
if (done) status = "ok";          // unbraced body: add braces (warning WIZZ-G026)
```

The same rules apply to inline `on:` handlers from compiler 1.17.1: `on:input={(e) => name = e.target.value}` is tracked, and from 1.23.0 so is the parenthesized `on:input={(e) => (name = e.target.value)}`, while `on:click={() => ok ? a = 1 : 0}` is not (the assignment sits inside an expression). From 1.23.0 every untracked assignment of a reactive name, in the script or a handler, is reported as warning WIZZ-G026 with its location; warnings never fail a build. Releases before 1.17.1 did not track assignments written directly in an inline handler; if `wizz --version` reports an older compiler, run `wizz update`.

- Use `const` for locals inside helper functions: the state scanner treats `let` declarations as component state.
- Reactive names may not be `__proto__` or start with `__wizz` (WIZZ-G017).
- Ordinary names are free at the top level of a script, including `target`, `props`, `state`, `update`, and `value`. Reserved there, and as prop or import names (WIZZ-G025): `__wizz`-prefixed names, `onMount`, `onDestroy`, `document`, `console`, `queueMicrotask`, `Array`, `Error`, `JSON`, `Map`, `Object`, `Set`, and `String`. Inside a function or block any name is allowed.
- Generated code is private: a script cannot read `target`, `props`, or any other generated name, so pass what it needs as a prop. Before 1.20.0, top-level names such as `target` and `state` could break the module or render a wrong value; if `wizz --version` reports an older compiler, run `wizz update`.

Derived values: Wizz has no computed syntax. Keep one function that recomputes derived state, call it after relevant changes and once in `onMount`.

```js
let items = [];
let total = 0;
let summary = "Cart is empty";

function recompute() {
  total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);
  summary = items.length === 0 ? "Cart is empty" : items.length + " items";
}

function add(item) {
  items = [...items, item];
  recompute();
}

onMount(recompute);
```

---

## 8. Events

`on:<event>` binds any native DOM event with `addEventListener`. The value is a component function, or an expression whose value is passed to `addEventListener`.

```html
<form on:submit={handleSubmit}>
  <input value={query} on:input={handleInput} />
  <input value={name} on:input={(event) => name = event.target.value} />
  <button type="button" on:click={(event) => add(5)}>+5</button>
</form>
```

- Assignments inside an inline arrow or `function` handler update the DOM like assignments in script functions (compiler 1.17.1 and later; the parenthesized `(e) => (x = ...)` form from 1.23.0). Write each mutation as its own statement.

### Two-way bindings (1.23.0+)

```html
<input bind:value={food} />
<input type="number" bind:value={calories} />   <!-- number; empty field: null -->
<input type="checkbox" bind:checked={logged} />
<select bind:value={meal}>...</select>
```

- `bind:value` works on `<input>` (not checkbox, radio, or file), `<textarea>`, and `<select>`; `bind:checked` on `<input type="checkbox">`.
- It is sugar for `value={x}` plus an `on:input` (`on:change` for select and checkbox) handler that assigns `x`: it server-renders, hydrates, works inside `{#if}`, and writes `persist()` state through.
- The target must be a top-level `let` named directly (WIZZ-P063): not a prop, `const`, or `user.name`. A bound `<input>` needs a static `type`.
- Not on component tags, inside `{#each}` bodies, or `<wizz:head>`, and no `bind:group`/`bind:this` (WIZZ-P062). An explicit `value`/`checked` beside the binding is WIZZ-P064. Use `value={...}` + `on:input` there.
- A server-rendered `<textarea>`/`<select>` shows its bound value after hydration.
- An inline handler that assigns a prop is WIZZ-G015, the same as in the script (1.17.1 and later).
- Native elements only: never on component tags (WIZZ-G011). From 1.22.0, `on:` directives work inside `{#each}` bodies with the row's item binding in scope (`on:click={() => remove(item.id)}`); before 1.22.0 they failed with WIZZ-G006.
- Handlers are client-only. Server rendering skips them; hydration attaches them.
- Wizz removes every listener it attached when its owning row, `{#if}` branch, or component is destroyed. Listeners you add to `window`/`document` yourself must be removed in `onDestroy`.

---

## 9. Lists: `{#each}`

```html
<script>
  let todos = [
    { id: 1, title: "Read the contract", rowClass: "item is-done" },
    { id: 2, title: "Build a keyed list", rowClass: "item" }
  ];

  function removeTodo(id) {
    todos = todos.filter((todo) => todo.id !== id);
  }
</script>

<div class="todos">
  <ul>{#each todos as todo (todo.id)}<li class={todo.rowClass}><span>{todo.title}</span><button type="button" on:click={() => removeTodo(todo.id)}>×</button></li>{/each}</ul>
</div>
```

Every `{#each}` must:

1. Sit directly inside a native element (WIZZ-G002).
2. Have exactly one native root element per row (WIZZ-G003).
3. Iterate a top-level `let` to update on reassignment (a `const` renders once).
4. Name the collection with a bare identifier: `{#each state.items as item}` and an index alias (`item, i`) are WIZZ-P002. Copy into a top-level `let` and store any index you need on the items.

Row bodies may NOT contain:

- Imported components (WIZZ-G004)
- Nested `{#if}` or `{#each}` (WIZZ-G005): precompute per-row classes and labels in the script

Row event handlers (1.22.0+): `on:` directives anywhere in a row run with the item variable in scope. Write per-row handlers as inline arrows (`on:click={() => removeTodo(todo.id)}`), which read the latest item when a keyed row is updated with a replacement object; a factory call (`on:click={makeHandler(todo)}`) evaluates once when the row is created and keeps the first item value. Before 1.22.0, `on:` inside `{#each}` failed with WIZZ-G006 — on older compilers, attach one listener to the parent container and delegate with `event.target.closest("[data-id]")`.

Keys: `(item.id)` retains and moves nodes by key; duplicate keys throw. Omit the key for primitives or when position is identity enough (rows update by index).

---

## 10. Conditionals: `{#if}`

```html
{#if status === "ready"}
  <p>Ready.</p>
{:else}
  <p>Loading…</p>
{/if}
```

The condition uses the same expression grammar (section 3). From 1.22.0, whenever a reactive `let` or prop read by the condition changes, the test is re-evaluated on the next batched update and the branch is replaced in place when its truthiness changes: the old branch leaves the DOM along with its `on:` listeners, inner lists, and child components, and the new branch is built from current state. A condition that reads only `const` values is evaluated once at mount with no block overhead. Before 1.22.0, `{#if}` chose its branch once at mount and never swapped it later (and before 1.18.1, a reactive binding inside an untaken branch crashed the mount); if `wizz --version` reports an older compiler, run `wizz update`.

There is no `{:else if}` (WIZZ-P033): nest an `{#if}` inside `{:else}`. Because replacing a branch rebuilds its DOM, internal DOM state inside a swapped branch (typed input text, scroll position, a child component's own state) is not preserved — when an element should stay mounted while hidden, toggle `hidden={closed}` or a bound class:

```html
<script>
  let open = false;
  let closed = true;

  function toggle() {
    open = !open;
    closed = !open;
  }
</script>

<section class="disclosure">
  <button on:click={toggle} aria-expanded={open}>Details</button>
  <div class="panel" hidden={closed}>Kept in the DOM while hidden.</div>
</section>
```

---

## 11. Script globals (no import)

- `onMount(callback)`: runs once, client-side, after the component is attached, children are mounted, and the initial update has run. May be async. The place for `window`, `document`, the URL, timers, observers, and fetches.
- `onDestroy(callback)`: runs on `destroy()`, before children are destroyed and the root is removed. Clean up here; do not change state.
- `persist(key, default)`: initializer for a top-level `let`.

```html
<script>
  let theme = persist("theme", "light");

  function toggle() {
    theme = theme === "light" ? "dark" : "light";
  }
</script>

<main>
  <button on:click={toggle}>Theme: {theme}</button>
</main>
```

`persist()` rules:

- Top-level `let` only. Not on a prop (P044), a `const` (P045), or nested (P046/P051).
- The key must be a string literal (P050), used verbatim as the `localStorage` key. Two components using the same key share state on purpose.
- Mount: the stored JSON value wins over the default. Every statement mutation writes back. Tabs sync over BroadcastChannel (storage events as fallback).
- SSR renders the default and hydration restores the stored value, so derive dependent values in `onMount`.

Read browser-only APIs inside `onMount` so the server render and the hydration walk agree:

```js
let userId = "";

onMount(() => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(document.location.search);
  userId = params.get("id") ?? "";
});
```

---

## 12. Styles and head

`<wizz:style>`: raw CSS, scoped by a generated `data-wizz-s` attribute on each selector's terminal element. `@keyframes` names gain the scope suffix. No expressions inside CSS (WIZZ-P017). Extracted into `dist/wizz.css` at build time, and linked from the built shell; built modules then carry no CSS of their own. Put global tokens and resets in `App.css`.

`<wizz:head>`: only `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`. Expressions evaluate at render time; the head follows navigation, not state (no reactive head updates). With several titles mounted, the last in tree order wins. Keep `index.html` free of its own `<title>`.

```html
<wizz:head>
  <title>{post.title} — My Blog</title>
  <meta name="description" content={post.summary}>
  <link rel="canonical" href={post.url}>
</wizz:head>
```

---

## 13. Routing

Routes come from the file system. Paths are lowercased; `index.wizz` names its directory.

```text
src/App.wizz                         ->  /
src/pages/index.wizz                 ->  /    (only one of these two may exist)
src/pages/Home.wizz                  ->  /home
src/pages/Admin/Users.wizz           ->  /admin/users
src/pages/docs/getting-started.wizz  ->  /docs/getting-started
```

- Matching is exact. There are no dynamic segments like `/users/:id`; use query strings read in `onMount`.
- Reserved prefixes: `/api`, `/runtime`, `/server`. Route collisions fail the build.
- Links are ordinary `<a href>` document navigations; the server renders the next page and the router hydrates it. Cross-document View Transitions (`@view-transition { navigation: auto; }`) work with no JavaScript.
- No router guard hook: protect data in server handlers and redirect from the page in `onMount`.
- Unmatched paths render `<main>Not found</main>`. Unmatched `/api/*` paths answer 404 JSON.

---

## 14. Server API routes

Code that must stay private (API keys, database calls) lives in `src/server/api/*.js`. Everything in a `.wizz` script ships to the browser.

```js
// src/server/api/greet.js → /api/greet
export default async function handler(request) {
  if (request.method !== "GET") {
    return { status: 405, headers: { allow: "GET" }, body: { error: "Method not allowed" } };
  }
  const name = (request.query.get("name") ?? "").trim().slice(0, 40) || "friend";
  return { message: "Hello, " + name + "!" };
}
```

File → route: `health.js` → `/api/health`, `index.js` → `/api`, `users/search.js` → `/api/users/search`. Files and directories starting with `_` are importable helpers, never routes.

`request` is a frozen object: `method`, `path` (decoded), `query` (`URLSearchParams`), `headers` (lowercased names), `body` (raw text or `null`, max 1 MB → 413), `json()` (async; malformed JSON → 400).

| Handler returns | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Plain value (object, array, number…) | 200 JSON |
| String | 200 plain text |
| `undefined` | 204 |
| `{ status, headers, body }` | Full control |
| Thrown error | Fixed 500 `{"error":"Internal server error"}` |

Secrets go in a gitignored `.env.server` at the project root (`KEY=VALUE` lines), never in `src/` or a `.wizz` file. Handlers read `process.env` at request time. Call handlers from components with ordinary `fetch("/api/...")`.

---

## 15. Server rendering and hydration

Pages server-render by default. The server calls the page's `renderComponent()`, puts the HTML in `#app`, places an `application/wizz-state` script beside it, and the router hydrates instead of re-rendering. On any hydration mismatch it warns once and remounts cleanly.

Server-renderable: static markup, text and attribute expressions, props, the initially taken `{#if}` branch, `{#each}`, and imported components (recursively, if each child is renderable). Event handlers and lifecycle hooks are client-only. Author scripts run on the server, so reading browser globals at the top level of a script breaks SSR: use `onMount`.

Built modules carry no CSS when the shell links `/wizz.css`, which `wizz build` arranges. An application that serves them from its own HTML instead of the built shell must link `/wizz.css` from that document, or pages arrive unstyled.

---

## 16. CLI

```bash
wizz init [dir] [--force] [--sample | --bare]   # scaffold; asks sample or bare on a TTY (1.24.0+)
wizz dev [--port <n>] [--host <addr>]  # build, serve 127.0.0.1:3000, watch, SSR, live reload
wizz build [in out] [--json] [--adapter node]
wizz mcp [--root <dir>] [--allow-write]
wizz update
wizz install-vscode-extension
wizz --version
```

- `wizz init` (1.24.0+) asks `Bootstrap with sample code? [Y/n]` only when stdin is a TTY and neither `--json`, `--sample`, nor `--bare` is given. Enter/`y`/`yes` → sample, `n`/`no` → bare, anything else re-asks; Ctrl+C (exit 130) or EOF (exit 1) writes nothing. `--sample` and `--bare` are mutually exclusive. It refuses a non-empty directory without `--force` and never overwrites a file.
- `wizz build` compiles every file (continuing past failures), writes route/API manifests, copies the runtime, `index.html`, `App.css`, and `src/server/`, and extracts styles to `dist/wizz.css`. Non-zero exit on any failure.
- `wizz build --json` prints a `wizz-build-diagnostics@1` envelope: `{ format, ok, diagnostics: [{ code, severity, message, file, line, column }], files: [{ file, serverRenderable }] }`.
- `wizz build --adapter node` adds `dist/server.mjs`, a standalone SSR + API host (`node dist/server.mjs`, default port 8080, `PORT` env).

---

## 17. MCP server (`wizz mcp`)

A zero-dependency MCP server over stdio. Register it with `{ "command": "wizz", "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/path/to/project", "--allow-write"] }`.

| Tool | Writes? | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project_overview` | No | Components, routes, API routes, versions, and the template-limits summary. Start here. |
| `language_contract` | No | The `.wizz` language contract, diagnostic catalog, and the template-limits table with working patterns. |
| `component_diagnostics` | No | Compile a file, inline source, or everything into structured records. |
| `create_or_update_component` | Yes (needs `--allow-write`) | Write a `.wizz` file only if it compiles. |
| `build_project` | `dist/` only | Run the build, return the JSON envelope. |
| `dev_workflow` | No | Dev/build/deploy commands and the secrets rule. |

Recommended loop: `project_overview` → `language_contract` → draft and check with `component_diagnostics` (inline `source`) → fix by switching on the diagnostic `code` and line/column → write with `create_or_update_component` → verify with `build_project`.

From compiler 1.17.1 both `project_overview` and `language_contract` return the template-language limits table: one row per area (expressions, `{#if}`, `{#each}` collection and body, dynamic attributes, quoted values, event handlers, component tags) with what is supported, the limit, how it fails (a diagnostic code, or "Silent" when it compiles but does not update), and the working pattern. It is plain text and also `structuredContent.templateLimits`, an array of `{ area, supported, limit, failure, workaround }`. Rows marked Silent are the ones to design around before writing code, because the compiler will not flag them.

---

## 18. Diagnostic codes

Codes are stable: never reworded into a different meaning or reused. `WIZZ-A###` is reserved and empty.

Most common:

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WIZZ-G001 | Template has no root element | Wrap content in one native element |
| WIZZ-P013 / P014 | Duplicate `<wizz:head>` / `<wizz:style>` | Merge the blocks |
| WIZZ-P020 | Plain `<style>` | Use `<wizz:style>` |
| WIZZ-P033 | Template expression error (indexing, `==`, `??`, arrow functions, ...) | Compute in the script or call a script function |
| WIZZ-P056 / P060 | `++`/`--`, or a code-from-string sink, in an expression | Mutate in a handler |
| WIZZ-P062 / P063 / P064 | Unsupported binding / invalid binding target / conflicting attribute | `value={...}` + `on:input`, or bind a top-level `let` |
| WIZZ-G026 (warning) | Reactive name assigned where no update is scheduled | Make the assignment its own statement; brace `if` bodies |
| WIZZ-G002 | `{#each}` outside a native element | Wrap the block |
| WIZZ-G003 | `{#each}` body needs one root element | Wrap the row |
| WIZZ-G004 | Component inside `{#each}` | Native markup in rows |
| WIZZ-G005 | Nested block inside `{#each}` | Precompute row values |
| WIZZ-G006 | Retired in 1.22.0 (was: `on:` inside `{#each}`) | Supported in 1.22.0+; upgrade or delegate from the container |
| WIZZ-G008 | Children on a component tag | Pass props |
| WIZZ-G010 | Component tag outside a native element | Wrap the tag |
| WIZZ-G011 | `on:` on a component tag | Pass a callback prop |
| WIZZ-G015 | Assignment to a prop | Copy into a local `let` |
| WIZZ-G016 | Imports not on their own lines | One import per line |

Parse stage (WIZZ-P): P001 tokenizer error · P002 malformed `{#each}` · P003 unexpected `{/each}` · P004 unexpected `{/if}` · P005 unexpected `{:else}` · P006 disallowed child in `<title>` · P007 disallowed element in `<wizz:head>` · P008 element in `<wizz:style>` · P009 attributes on `<wizz:head>` · P010 nested `<wizz:head>` · P011 attributes on `<wizz:style>` · P012 nested `<wizz:style>` · P013 duplicate `<wizz:head>` · P014 duplicate `<wizz:style>` · P015 block directive in `<wizz:head>` · P016 expression directly in `<wizz:head>` · P017 expression in `<wizz:style>` · P018 mismatched closing tag · P019 only title/meta/link in head · P020 plain `<style>` · P021 closing tag on void element · P022 unclosed tag · P023 unexpected closing tag · P024 unsupported token · P025 unclosed string in expression · P026 unexpected character in expression · P027 unparseable expression start · P028 expected `)` · P029 expected property after `.` · P030 unexpected expression token · P031 missing `{#if}` condition · P032 dynamic attribute missing expression · P033 template expression error · P034 invalid prop name · P035 reserved prop prefix `__wizz` · P036 `export let` without a name · P037 `export` not at top level · P038 one prop per `export let` · P039 invalid prop declaration · P040 duplicate prop · P041 prop missing value · P042 prop missing semicolon · P043 unsupported export syntax · P044 `persist()` on a prop · P045 `persist()` on a const · P046 `persist()` not top level · P047 statements trailing a `persist()` declaration · P048 `persist()` missing arguments · P049 `persist()` extra arguments · P050 `persist()` key not a string literal · P051 nested `persist()` · P052 unparseable `persist()` call · P053 expression depth budget exceeded · P054 template depth budget exceeded · P055 interpolation inside a quoted attribute value (1.22.1+) · P056 `++`/`--` in an expression · P057 number or string literal a module cannot load · P058 conditional missing `:` · P059 calling something other than a name or method · P060 code-from-string sink in an expression that calls · P061 reserved word as a name · P062 unsupported binding · P063 invalid binding target · P064 conflicting binding (P056–P064: 1.23.0+).

Generate stage (WIZZ-G): G001 no root element · G002 `{#each}` outside native element · G003 `{#each}` body needs one root · G004 component in `{#each}` · G005 unsupported node in `{#each}` (nested blocks) · G006 retired in 1.22.0 (was: `on:` in `{#each}`) · G007 invalid prop attribute name · G008 children on component tag · G009 component missing id (internal) · G010 component tag outside native element · G011 `on:` on component tag · G012 event directive missing handler · G013 invalid event directive · G014 disallowed child in `<title>` · G015 assignment to a prop · G016 imports must be on their own lines · G017 reserved reactive name · G018 server build: unsupported node · G019 server build: unsupported head node · G020 server build: component not server-renderable · G021 void element with children · G022 hydration: unsupported node · G023 hydration: unsupported node in `{#each}` · G024 `persist()` rewrite drift (internal) · G025 reserved top-level, prop, or import name · G026 warning: reactive name assigned where no update is scheduled (1.23.0+).

---

## 19. Habits from other frameworks that fail

| You might write | Wizz.js equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| `{items[0]}`, `{list.map(...)}`, `{a ?? b}` | Compute in `<script>` and render the name, or call a script function: `{first(items)}` (1.23.0+) |
| `class="btn {variant}"` | `class={"btn " + variant}`, or `let btnClass = "btn " + variant;` then `class={btnClass}` |
| `hidden={!open}` | Valid from 1.23.0 (1.21.0+ removes the attribute when falsy). Before 1.23.0, compute `let closed = !open;` and write `hidden={closed}` |
| `v-model` / `bind:value` on a component or in `{#each}` | `bind:value={name}` on a native `<input>`/`<textarea>`/`<select>` (1.23.0+); in rows or on components, `value={...}` plus an `on:input` handler |
| `{:else if b}` | Nest `{#if b}` inside `{:else}` |
| `<Card><p>Body</p></Card>` / `<slot>` | `<Card body="..." />` or compose native elements around the tag |
| `<Child on:save={fn} />` / `@save` / `onSave` event emit | Callback prop: `<Child onSave={fn} />`, child calls `onSave(value)` |
| `{#each}` row with a component (`<Row item={item} />`) | Native row markup (`on:click={() => fn(item.id)}` on native elements inside `{#each}` works in 1.22.0+; on older compilers use a delegated listener on the parent) |
| `items.push(x)` | `items = [...items, x];` |
| `$:` reactive statements, `computed`, `useMemo` | A `recompute()` function called after changes and in `onMount` |
| `useState`, `ref()`, `$state` | Top-level `let` |
| `import { onMount } from "..."` | Just call `onMount(...)`: it is a compiler global |
| `window.x` at the top of `<script>` | Read it inside `onMount` |
| `/users/[id].wizz`, `/users/:id` | Exact routes only: `/user?id=42` read in `onMount` |
| `<style>` | `<wizz:style>` |
| Two sibling root elements | One wrapping native element |

---

## 20. Complete example

```html
<script>
  import Badge from "./components/Badge.wizz";

  let draft = "";
  let nextId = 3;
  let tasks = persist("tasks", [
    { id: 1, title: "Read the contract", done: true, rowClass: "task is-done" },
    { id: 2, title: "Build a keyed list", done: false, rowClass: "task" }
  ]);
  let remaining = 0;
  let remainingLabel = "0 left";

  function recompute() {
    remaining = tasks.filter((task) => !task.done).length;
    remainingLabel = remaining + " left";
  }

  function handleDraft(event) {
    draft = event.target.value;
  }

  function addTask(event) {
    event.preventDefault();
    const title = draft.trim();
    if (!title) return;
    tasks = [...tasks, { id: nextId, title, done: false, rowClass: "task" }];
    nextId += 1;
    draft = "";
    recompute();
  }

  function handleListClick(event) {
    const row = event.target.closest("[data-id]");
    if (!row) return;
    const id = Number(row.dataset.id);
    tasks = tasks.map((task) => {
      if (task.id !== id) return task;
      const done = !task.done;
      return { ...task, done, rowClass: done ? "task is-done" : "task" };
    });
    recompute();
  }

  onMount(() => {
    nextId = Math.max(0, ...tasks.map((task) => task.id)) + 1;
    recompute();
  });
</script>

<wizz:head>
  <title>Tasks</title>
</wizz:head>

<main class="tasks">
  <h1>Tasks</h1>
  <form class="add" on:submit={addTask}>
    <input value={draft} on:input={handleDraft} placeholder="New task" aria-label="New task" />
    <button type="submit">Add</button>
  </form>
  <ul class="list" on:click={handleListClick}>{#each tasks as task (task.id)}<li class={task.rowClass} data-id={task.id}>{task.title}</li>{/each}</ul>
  <footer class="foot">
    <Badge label={remainingLabel} />
  </footer>
</main>

<wizz:style>
  .tasks { display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-inline-size: 32rem; margin-inline: auto; }
  .foot { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; }
  .add { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; }
  .list { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
  .task { padding-block: 0.5rem; cursor: pointer; }
  .task.is-done { opacity: 0.5; text-decoration: line-through; }
</wizz:style>
```

```html
<!-- src/components/Badge.wizz -->
<script>
  export let label = "New";
</script>

<span class="badge">{label}</span>

<wizz:style>
  .badge { padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #eee; font-size: 0.85rem; }
</wizz:style>
